**MassifScript: the terrain graph as text, and a guide for any AI**

The Terrain Generator's graph can now be read and written as a script, in a small C-like language of its own: `base = FractalNoise(scale: 2400, height: 600);` makes a node, `eroded = StreamErosion(base);` feeds another, `group "Geology" { … }` frames them, `output height = eroded;` sends the relief to the map, and components, constants, conditions, loops and imports build more at once. The script button beside the graph shows it as a script that follows the graph; what you type is checked as you type, mistakes underlined with their line and column and the name you probably meant, and Apply makes the graph from it in one step you can undo, the nodes you had keeping their places. A script makes exactly the nodes, links, frames and composites the editor makes, and every graph can be written back as a script. Copy for AI copies a guide to paste into any AI chat (every node with its settings, examples and your graph), so that it can answer with a script to paste and apply. `.mscript` files open and save from the pane, and `massif-cli mscript guide`, `build`, `check` and `decompile` do the same from the command line.
